summary: Autoreleasepool push/pop/drain behavior is runtime-owned: pushes create isolated stack frames, autorelease enqueues into the current frame, and pop drains only the top frame before the enclosing frame can drain.
drain_order_rule: nested pool frames drain innermost before outermost
each popped frame drains values in reverse enqueue order
managed receivers queued into each frame are destroyed by that frame pop
autorelease outside an explicit pool continues through the dispatch-frame autorelease queue
expected_runtime_order: pop and drain inner values newest-first and destroy the inner managed receiver
pop and drain outer values newest-first and destroy the outer managed receiver
validation_needed: run the narrow runtime autoreleasepool probes that inspect nested queue and last-drained state
run the issue-level acceptance command after parallel #8035 lowering edits settle
